turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Doctor, this is Mr Vos. His wife brought him in and she's waiting by the cars — she asked me to pass on what she's been noticing.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you, Sister. Mr Vos, come and sit. How are you keeping?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Good morning, Doctor. I am quite well, thank you. I must say I do not entirely see why we are here.
[SEG0004] person_1 (NURSE): His wife says he repeats the same questions, over and over, and it's been a few months now. He's missed appointments as well.
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): With respect, Sister, that is not correct. I do not repeat myself. My wife is inclined to fuss.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): I hear you. In your own words, how have things been at home?
[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): Perfectly ordinary, Doctor. I read the paper, I walk to the shops, I potter in the garden. I am seventy-six, not a child.
[SEG0008] person_1 (NURSE): She was quite upset about last Tuesday. She says he got lost coming back from Checkers and was gone nearly two hours.
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): I was not lost. I stopped beside the robot at the garage to greet an old colleague from the municipality. I knew precisely where I was.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): And did you get home on your own, or did someone come and fetch you?
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): I walked home myself. It merely took longer than my wife expected.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): What about those appointments she mentioned. Has anything slipped your mind?
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Nothing has slipped. My diary is kept in good order.
[SEG0014] person_1 (NURSE): Sorry, Doctor, the wife left the clinic card with me. The blood pressure review in March and the eye test in April are both marked did not attend.
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): Ah, well, the eye test I will concede I forgot. The blood pressure visit I had down for the following week. So that is two, if we are to be exact, and I do apologise.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): No apology needed. Any headaches, weakness down one side, or trouble finding your words?
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): No, none of those. My speech is as it has always been, and I have neither a headache nor any weakness.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): How are you sleeping, and how is your mood?
[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): I sleep well enough, and my mood is perfectly even. Nothing the matter there.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Anyone in the family who became forgetful as they grew older?
[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): My mother did, in her eighties. She would ask the same thing and then smile as if it were quite new. My father stayed sharp to the end.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): And at home, is it just the two of you?
[SEG0023] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes. We have shared the house in Rondebosch since I retired from the municipality. She runs the kitchen and, I should say, the medicines.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke at all, or take a drink?
[SEG0025] person_3 (PATIENT): I have never smoked. A single glass of wine on a Sunday, nothing more.
[SEG0026] person_1 (NURSE): She sets out every dose. Her note says amlodipine five milligrams in the morning, and a cholesterol tablet at night. She didn't write the name, only 'small white tablet'.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mr Vos, does that sound like what you actually take?

[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): The amlodipine, yes, five milligrams each morning, for my blood pressure, which I have had for years. The white tablet I swallow at night, because she says it is for my cholesterol. I am afraid I cannot tell you its name.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any operations in the past, or any allergy to a medicine?
[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): No operations, Doctor. And no allergies. None that I have ever been told of.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): When last were bloods done? Did anything come back that worried you?

[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): About three years ago, at the day hospital, they checked my cholesterol. They said it was borderline. They did not start a tablet then. The white one came later, though I cannot recall the year exactly.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Chest, tummy, waterworks — anything playing up?
[SEG0034] person_3 (PATIENT): No, Doctor. All of that is quite in order.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): May I have a quick look? Squeeze my fingers, both sides. Now just stand for me, there we go.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Grip is the same in both hands. You're steady on your feet. No swelling at the ankles.

[SEG0037] person_1 (NURSE): Vitals from just now. Blood pressure one hundred and fifty-two over eighty-eight, pulse seventy-six, temperature thirty-six point four, and his oxygen sat was ninety-eight percent.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you. Mr Vos, you were out for nearly two hours on Tuesday. I'd like to send you for a CT scan of the head, just to be on the safe side.

[SEG0039] person_3 (PATIENT): If you think it necessary, Doctor, I will of course attend. I must repeat, though, that I was not lost. And this is hardly new — my wife has been saying these things since last winter.
[SEG0040] person_1 (NURSE): Yes, that's what she told me as well. Months, not something sudden. No fall, and no knock to the head.
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ah, that changes things for me. If it's been creeping in since winter, and there's been no injury, I'm not going to send you for a scan today.

[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): What we'll do instead is bloods — full blood count, thyroid, vitamin B12, glucose and the kidney function — and I'll book a memory assessment at the clinic. I'm not putting a name to this today.
[SEG0043] person_3 (PATIENT): I am grateful. May I ask what the blood tests are looking for? I feel perfectly well.

[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): Just the ordinary things that can muddle a person's memory a little, like a low thyroid or a low B12. Even if those are fine, the memory assessment tells us where you stand. No label, and no fuss.
[SEG0045] person_3 (PATIENT): Very well. And the small white tablet — shall I continue with it?
[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, please carry on with both tablets, exactly as your wife sets them out. Next time, bring the boxes, so we can put a proper name to the white one.
[SEG0047] person_1 (NURSE): I can take the bloods straight after this, if you're happy. The memory clinic usually phones within a fortnight.
[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, please, Sister, do the bloods today. Mr Vos, come back and see me once we have the blood results and the memory clinic has seen you.
[SEG0049] person_3 (PATIENT): I shall do so. My wife will insist on coming with me, which is very much her way.
[SEG0050] person_2 (DOCTOR): She's very welcome. If you do go walking, stick to your usual route, and just let her know when you set out. That's all I ask.
[SEG0051] person_3 (PATIENT): That is perfectly reasonable. Thank you for your patience, Doctor, and you as well, Sister.
[SEG0052] person_1 (NURSE): I'll get the forms. You can sit with your wife, Mr Vos, she's just outside.
